Question: Two points \(B\) and \(C\) are in a plane. Let \(S\) be the set of all points \(A\) in the plane for which \(\triangle ABC\) has area \(1.\) Which of the following describes \(S?\)
Solution:
Assume first that \(B\) and \(C\) are distinct, as is usual when they form the base of a triangle. Let \(L=BC>0\). With this fixed base, the area depends only on the perpendicular distance \(h\) from \(A\) to the full line through \(B\) and \(C\). The area condition gives
\[
\frac12 Lh=1,
\qquad h=\frac{2}{L}>0.
\]
On each side of line \(BC\), all points at this fixed perpendicular distance form a line parallel to \(BC\). Every point on either parallel gives the required height and hence area \(1\). Conversely, every point giving area \(1\) must have this height, so it lies on one of these two parallels. The perpendicular foot may lie outside segment \(BC\), so the parallels extend indefinitely.

Thus, for distinct \(B\) and \(C\), the set is two parallel lines, choice \(\mathrm{A}\).

If \(B=C\), the base has length zero and no choice of \(A\) gives area \(1\). In that case \(S\) is empty, which is not among the listed choices.
